Computer vision is a field of artificial intelligence that allows computers to see and understand images and videos. Instead of just taking a picture, the computer uses special programs to analyze the pixels and find patterns. This enables two main tasks: image recognition, which means identifying what is in a photo (like a cat or a tree), and object detection, which goes further by finding the location of multiple objects in the same frame.

These abilities have many real-world applications. For example, in medicine, computer vision helps doctors spot diseases in X-rays. In security, it can monitor crowds or verify identities. Perhaps the most exciting use is in self-driving cars. With cameras and computer vision, these vehicles can recognize traffic signs, pedestrians, and other cars instantly. This information helps the car decide when to stop or turn, making driving safer. As technology improves, computer vision will continue changing how we interact with the world around us.
